title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Local Climate Regulation"
format:

---

Local climate regulation is urban cooling. Vegetation lowers city temperatures, buildings spend
less electricity on air conditioning, and the account values that saved electricity. The base year
is 2019 and the price convention recorded in `es_config.csv` is `avoided energy cost`.

## Quantity

InVEST urban cooling gives each city-month a vegetation cooling effect, which the chain converts
into an electricity difference in kilowatt-hours, the `kwh_diff` column of the committed
city-month files.

The cooling-degree measure behind that conversion is `temp_degc_to_cdd_smooth`, v04's smoothed
exceedance. Below the base minus the window it returns zero, above the base plus the window it is
linear in temperature, and across the window it follows `smoothstep01`, the cubic
$t^2(3-2t)$ on [0, 1].

## Price

The national electricity price in USD per kilowatt-hour, the `price_usd_per_kwh` column.

## Valuation

$$
\text{total\_savings\_usd} = \text{kwh\_diff} \times \text{price\_usd\_per\_kwh}
$$

`city_savings_identity` recomputes that product at rtol 1e-6 and raises if it breaks. Summing
cities to countries gives the December 2025 version of the accounting table.

The current final applies v04's correction, written explicitly in that version's code and ported
verbatim in `apply_country_marginal_consumption`. It divides out the old global
marginal-consumption slope embedded in the v02 values and multiplies by each country's own
consumption per cooling-degree-day, which is cooling energy per capita over the IEA-CMCC 2019
humid-CDD total.

$$
\text{corrected} = \frac{\text{value}}{\text{URBAN\_COOLING\_OLD\_GLOBAL\_MC}} \times \text{consumption per CDD}
$$

## What the library reports

`gep_calculation` reads the committed final table, parses its dollar-formatted string column
through `parse_dollar_column`, and joins it onto the r250 country list by label.

Three things verify against staged data. The kilowatt-hour times price identity is exact. The
merged-sum identity against the December 2025 version is exact on every country tested. The
current final's parse and totals check out.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `local_climate_regulation` service:

- `local_climate_regulation_final_path`, the committed final accounting table.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, and `local_climate_regulation_gep`.

## Method constants

- `URBAN_COOLING_OLD_GLOBAL_MC = 1.71737465916468`, the old global marginal-consumption slope that
  v04 divides out.
- `URBAN_COOLING_CDD_BASE_C = 18.0`, the humid cooling-degree-day base the chain uses (CDDhum18).
- `URBAN_COOLING_SMOOTH_WINDOW_C = 1.0`, the width of the smoothing window either side of the base.

## Taken as given

The InVEST urban cooling run itself and the national electricity prices.

## What is open

The v04 correction's own inputs are not reproducible here. The IEA-CMCC cooling-degree-day file
and the v2_nkd energy workbook live only on the author's machine, and the staged VERSION4 energy
CSV is a different vintage that does not validate the inversion. Those two files are the named
asks.
